result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B gives the actual reason in plain words: gaps between letters grow with the letters, so big headlines look loose and gappy. It also shows the reader what goes wrong if you tighten paragraph text, since the letters 'run together'. A is accurate and shorter, but its 'viewed from a distance' explanation is less direct about why size matters, and 'harder to read' is vaguer; B loses only a little for its 'Here's a draft' lead-in line. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A gives the real reason in plain words: gaps grow along with the letters, so big headlines look loose and gappy, while paragraph text is already spaced to read well and tightening it would make the letters run together. B is shorter, but it puts the problem down to uneven gaps seen from a distance rather than gaps that grow with size, and its picture of what goes wrong is less concrete. A's one-line 'Here's a draft you can paste' lead-in costs it a little on length, but the pasteable message itself is three sentences.
